channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [7] Nano-wrinkle waveguides for programmable polariton channeling
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Peining Li, Qing Dai

Authors: Liyan Wang, Bei Yang, Tian Sun, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of polaritons in van der Waals materials, relevant to 2D physics.

Tags: #polaritons #nanophotonics #vanderWaalsmaterials

Abstract: Polaritons (hybrid light-matter excitations) in van der Waals materials hold promise for nanophotonics, but their application is normally hampered by their limited lateral confinement. Here, the authors report a strategy to fabricate deterministic high- curvature wrinkles in hBN films and apply them as controllable polaritonic and thermal waveguides.
